title: quiz grading spec
description: Binary criteria over an answer space, grouped in tiers that never trade off, and the records that placed them.

version.description: The grammar version this spec is written in; changelog.md lists each.

instruction.description: The task as the answerer reads it.

as_of.description: The date the facts hold at.

scope.description: What a complete answer covers, so two experts agree on it.

deliverable.description: What the answer is and who reads it.

evidence_goal.description: What a grade must show about an answer.

source.description: The url or path of the rubric this spec was migrated from.

group_size.description: Answers graded together per prompt in training; 8 when absent.

tiers.description: Highest first; a lower tier never buys back a higher one.

exchange.description: The exchange tests that placed each criterion.

mode.description: The judge grades every criterion in one call, with the whole rubric in view.

estimated.description: True while each judge_error is an estimate, not measured on human labels.

monitor.description: Signals watched while the spec is in use.

delta.description: The smallest expected tier-score difference no lower tier may overturn.

judge_error.description: The chance the judge flips one verdict of this tier.

mask_below.description: When this tier scores below pass, every lower tier scores 0.

pass_rate.description: The expected share of answers that pass a masked tier.

pass.description: The tier score a masked tier needs; 1 when absent.

pairwise.description: The last tier: quality no criterion captures, scored by within-group wins.

text.description: One observable proposition about the answer.

polarity.description: - when the proposition is an error the answer commits.

anchors.description: What a vague word in the text means here.

variants_ok.description: Valid answers the criterion must pass.

source.description: Where it came from: a url, a path or the failure in words.
